newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh buys 100,000T wheat at $188.44/T CIF.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh buys 100,000T wheat at $188.44/T CIF.

text.p: Bangladesh on Wednesday said a deal for buying 100,000 tonnes of wheat had been delayed for a week due to a disagreement over the origin of the cargo.
"We have bought 100,000 tonnes of wheat and already awarded the deal to a company and gave the supplier one week's time to come to terms on specification," said one government official.

He said: "We have asked the company to supply us hard red winter/spring wheat of U.S. origin but the firm wants us to accept Australian wheat. Both the varieties are in the option list in the tender document."
Food ministry officials said a high level committee awarded the deal to Romak of St Louis in the U.S. at a CIF price of $188.44 a tonne for shipment by February 10.
The local agent of the U.S. company was not available for comments.
